page: Microsoft Azure EC2ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 execution threads, coupled with 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB, delivering an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Local ephemeral storage includes an 81 GB solid-state drive, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor without bundled GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data displays strong single-core CPU throughput, where stress-ng single-core performance registers in the top 25 percent at 3016.26. Geekbench single-core reaches 1860.0 and text processing scores 2043.0, both placing in the middle 50 percent tier alongside PassMark memory performance at 1847.43. However, due to its low total core allocation of a single physical core, multi-threaded metrics remain limited. Both stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core place in the lower 25 percent, while compiling software with clang and PassMark database operations land in the bottom 10 percent.

This instance profile offers cost efficiency for memory-centric, low-concurrency operations rather than parallel compute execution. The provision of 16.0 GB of memory paired with an 81 GB local SSD makes it suitable for intermediate memory caching, small relational databases, staging environments, and single-threaded or lightly threaded backend tasks requiring high memory density per vCPU.
description: Microsoft Azure EC2ads_v6 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single AMD EPYC 9V74 physical core on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a generous 8.0 GB per core allocation alongside an 81 GB local SSD for temporary storage. While stress-ng single-core execution demonstrates strong performance within the top 25 percent and memory subsystem benchmarks achieve average marks, total parallel compute capacity is constrained by the two-thread limit, as reflected in lower-tier Geekbench and PassMark multi-core results. The instance contains no GPU acceleration and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With its high RAM-to-CPU ratio and integrated local solid-state storage, this configuration is best deployed for lightweight in-memory caching, small transactional databases, and low-concurrency backend services.
